items.en: "Whatever your other, lesser accomplishments, there is one in particular which is why you are here. The ship is in your fleet - what is known to history as the Onslaught Mk.I, which is of interest to me."

She pauses a moment, eyes black.

"I shall make my proposal shortly. First, allow me to elaborate on a shape for our partnership."
"You know my title. I take a portion of surplus capital from the Company and invest it in what we like to call 'black sky initiatives'."

"There are unimaginable possibilities out there." She raises an arm, hand extended, fingers like rays into the far, dark corners of the cavernous office.

You sense the lights dim slightly - a dramatic effect triggered by her cybernetic implants, no doubt.

"I take the very long shots. There are things," she stresses the word oddly, "Such things out there, captain. Technologies and phenomena the Human Domain hid away, and from. They locked such wonders and treasures up in red-tape concocted by fearful, jealous little minds. They suffocated these opportunities, blinded themselves to unimaginable possibilities."

"The returns from exploitation would be... astronomical. Or perhaps," her eyes glint in the filtered starlight, "They may prove to be of value well beyond that of mere stars."

Her head gives a small twitch.

"Regret, you say."

"I see," she says.

"You found them. In the Abyss. And returned." The Director pauses a moment. "This simply proves your fitness for the operation."

"Evidently, you already have," she says.

"This simply proves your fitness for the operation."
"It is," she smiles, teeth jewel-like. "And I'll ensure that you receive your share."
"Then I think we shall work well together," she says.
"Yes. Does that frighten you?" she asks.

She pauses a moment, making no outward reaction to your bravado.

"I see," she allows, finally.

She pauses a moment, making no outward reaction to your pretense of bravado.

"I see," she allows, finally.

"I see," she says after a moment.

"I trust that you shall ensure your executive judgment is merely tempered, not impaired, by such sentiment."
"Of course," she says, allowing a trace of amusement to enter her voice.
She makes no outward reaction to your implication, simply proceeding as if you'd said nothing at all.

"The Perseus-Orion Abyss is a melodramatic name. I find spacers are a superstitious lot, present company excepted. Self-limiting mythology is best discarded if one means to ascend to the fullest of human potential." She looks away for a moment, making a dismissive flick with her flingers.

"You know of the Perseus-Orion Abyss? A melodramatic name. I find spacers are a superstitious lot, excepting present company. Self-limiting mythology is best discarded if one means to ascend to the fullest of human potential." She looks away for a moment, making a dismissive flick with her flingers.

"It is true, however, that the Abyss is hostile to our hyperspace technology. That is precisely why the secrets it holds may be all the more profitably disruptive."

She turns to look you full-on, once more. "I want you to go there. I have data... there is something to find. Very old. Very dangerous. Very valuable. Bring me scans, samples. You will be paid handsomely for tangible specimens."

"You know the Perseus-Orion Abyss. You went there, and there you found the Onslaught Mk.I... and the 'Threat'."

She looks at you anew, more present somehow.

"I very much desire to have a look at the Mk.I."

"You know the Perseus-Orion Abyss. You know of the 'Threat'." She looks away. "A typically non-descriptive name passed to us from some primitive government committee, I'm sure."

"You found Academician Cornelius Elek's enigma, the Onslaught Mk.I... among other things."

She looks at you anew, more present somehow.

"This is what I want."
"Not exactly," she says, self-satisifed. "Something more valuable."

"Those old things?" She gives her head an abbreviated shake. 

"No, we have people for that. Although," she fixes you with a look, "they've made quite a mess of it, haven't they? The wasted possibilities... but no, we're looking for something older... different."

"No, nothing like that." She emits a joyless laugh, like a machine, then pauses suddenly.

"Although if you did happen to find alien technology... provide me with exclusive access and I would ensure you credits enough to purchase your own solar system. Or," she waves a hand in an unconscious arc, "Build yourself a new one out of dross, if that's what you enjoy."
"There's no need. Our strategic indicators forecast a reasonably likely chance of your survival if your outlook is unbiased by speculation, so take heart." She trails off.

Sensing the insufficiency of her pep-talk, she begins anew: "What it is, is old. Early Domain. Pre-Persean Frontier, but we have reason to believe some part of it is out... here. Whether it followed us or we followed it. Whatever it is, wherever there is."
"Not exactly," she says, self-satisfied. "Something more valuable."

"Crews talk, TriPads listen. There is little I cannot know if I so wish," she says, injecting a tone of boredom into her words.

"Accept it. Now let's speak of business."

She laughs with a buzz like a malfunctioning agrav plate.

"Oh, no. That'd be far too provocative to..." She gives a little flick of the hand, indicating enemies too irrelevant to bother acknowledging in speech.

The Hegemony, maybe.

"However," she fixes upon you. "I would gladly pay for the opportunity to have my people take a close look at it. And take a few samples, very small, nothing damaging."

She blinks. "Detect them?"

Her voice is emotionless.

Her face arranges itself into a shape suggesting dismissive amusement.

"What an interesting theory, captain. Whatever my motives, will you agree to my proposal? A simple look, a few scans. A few samples."

A long pause. Her eyes flicker, accessing. Calculating.

"This is possible." She speaks with an emotion suddenly present - quiet displeasure, presumably at your maneuvering.

"You ask for much, captain."

"Done," she says, her voice as empty as the Abyss.

Almost instantly, your TriPad pings with several alerts - credits transfer, but also notification from your tactical officer concerning an approaching Tri-Tachyon portside-tender, swarming with engineering drones, and your comms, forwarding certain docking requests directly to the Onslaught Mk.I.

"Take a moment to ensure your affairs are in order, captain," Glamor-Rotanev says.

You'd think she enjoys overwhelming your officers with the speed of her response.

"Fine," she says, the spite cold in her voice.

"You've seen them. The Threat. Ancient, automated warfleets deep in the Abyss. And you lived." She is quite collected, suddenly, as she speaks.

"Would you part with recordings of your encounter with the Threat? I offer 100,000 credits for immediate transfer."

Director Glamor-Rotanev takes a moment to turn and appear to look out over her spectacular view of the Xanadu Geodivision.

You're certain she's watching her teams as they board the Onslaught Mk.I through what are no doubt top-of-the-line cybernetic implants and neural integrations.

And, doubtless, watching your comms. Because just as you are finished, she turns back, resettling her facial muscles with a twitch.

"As I was saying, I have a great interest in... specimens. Artifacts. Like yours. And like what I presume it was built to fight," she says. 

"You have been far more successful than the others. I would propose you repeat that success."

Her eyes flicker subtly, her expression more glazed and vacant than before.

"Very... good, captain," she says. Her words come more rapidly. "You've seen them. The Threat. Ancient, automated warfleets deep in the Abyss. And you lived."

"Would you part with recordings of your encounter with the Threat? I offer 100,000 credits for immediate transfer."
She says nothing, her disapproval resounding in the silence.
"A threat, presumably. The hostile connotation lives in the name." A quick, bloodless smile. "You'll prepare yourself for anything, I'm sure."

"We assume it'll engage in some sort of hostile action against you or your $shipOrFleet," she says indifferently. "Only this won't be pirate, Pather, or tariff patrol."

"Nor," she fixes you with a cool look, "Some remnant AI warfleet. Those, those we know about."

"Disappointing conversationalists," she mutters. "Superintelligence with no mind for business. Simply unbelievable..."

She blinks. Her eyes seem suddenly present for the first time. And she stares for several seconds, motionless.

"You're telling the truth," she says, outwardly cool.

"Would you part with recordings of your encounters with both of these... forces? I offer 150,000 credits for immediate transfer."
"So you are open to dealing," she says. "Good."
"You've been most useful," she says, almost actually smiling. It looks uncomfortable.

For a full two seconds her eyes close, moving rapidly.

Your TriPad pings.

She blinks. Her eyes seem suddenly present for the first time. 

"And you lived to tell it," she says, outwardly cool. You suspect, however, that you've impressed the Director because she pauses a moment to consider your words.

"Would you part with recordings of your encounter with the Threat? I offer 100,000 credits for immediate transfer."

For a full two seconds her eyes close, moving rapidly.

Your TriPad pings a credits transfer.

"Interesting," she says, and releases a breath. "Yes. This is what I am looking for."

She blinks. Her eyes seem suddenly present for the first time.

"That does not... quite fit with our working knowledge of the issue. Would you part with recordings of your... encounter with these entities? I offer 100,000 credits for immediate transfer."

For a full two seconds her eyes close, moving rapidly.

Your TriPad pings a credits transfer.

"Fascinating," she says, and releases a breath. "This is unlike previous reports."

"Perhaps," she says coldly, meaning 'perhaps not'.

"And disappointing. It would be useful to compare your data to our baseline. I must emphasize my interest - my financial interest - in procuring specimens of the type described."

"Perhaps," she says, repeating you rather frostily.

"And disappointing. It would be useful to compare your data to our baseline. I must emphasize my interest - my financial interest - in procuring more information about the Threat."

She blinks and her eyes seem suddenly present for the first time. And they narrow slightly.

"Of course not," she says. "But when you do, I'm sure you'll quickly realize why no one else in the Sector is prepared to deal seriously with this... Threat. It is in your interest to work with me."

"I insist that you spare no expense in outfitting your expedition. Bring more fuel and supplies than you anticipate needing so that you don't embarrass yourself like the- well, never mind them. You're a winner, and we place our bets on winners."

"'Was there another...' she says, repeating your words.

"Dozens! Some returned with nothing, others not at all. I won't conceal the fact from you. Maybe you'll find them, though don't feel compelled to render assistance on behalf of the Tri-Tachyon Corporation. These were independent contractors who accepted and assumed the risk. Then failed."

"If anything," she says quietly, "we have grounds to sue them if they ever manage to get back to the Core Worlds."
